claims.quote: Five such coaches were filled as I watched, and were shot up the guides to be locked on to their waiting packets three hundred feet nearer the stars.
claims.description: Airships carry mail in detachable coaches that are shot up guide rails from a tower and locked on mid-air to the packet.

claims.quote: Contrast this with the nine hundred by ninety-five of any crack liner, and you will realize the power that must drive a hull through all weathers at more than the emergency speed of the Cyclonic!
claims.description: Large passenger airliners about 900 feet long and fast mail airships operate routinely in all weather.

claims.quote: We know that Fleury's gas can lift anything, as the world-famous trials of '89 showed, but its almost indefinite powers of expansion necessitate vast tank room.
claims.description: A new lifting gas with enormous lift and expansion lets airships carry heavy loads.

claims.quote: Here we find Fleury's Paradox of the Bulk-headed Vacuum—which we accept now without thought—literally in full blast. The three engines are H.T.&T. assisted-vacuo Fleury turbines
claims.description: Turbine engines driven by gas that is condensed to liquid in a vacuum chamber by an electric 'Ray', then recycled to gas, power the airships.

claims.quote: Even Fleury who begat it and, unlike Magniac, died a multi-millionaire, could not explain how the restless little imp shuddering in the U-tube can, in the fractional fraction of a second, strike the furious blast of gas into a chill greyish-green liquid
claims.description: A radium-salt-fed 'Fleury's Ray' instantly liquefies gas in a vacuum tube and is a poorly understood heart of the engine.

claims.quote: Blessed be Sargent, Ahrens, and the Dubois brothers, who invented the cloud-breakers of the world whereby we travel in security!
claims.description: A worldwide network of powerful coloured beacons (cloud-breakers) pierces cloud layers to guide aerial navigation.

claims.quote: Our General Communication dial has caught her talk and begins to eavesdrop.
claims.description: Ships carry a wireless voice communicator that picks up other aircrafts' conversations and general calls over long distances.

claims.quote: Mail-packets are supposed, under the Conference rules, to have the five-thousand-foot lanes to themselves
claims.description: International agreements assign altitude lanes in the sky to different classes of air traffic.

claims.quote: Magniac invented his rudder to help war-boats ram each other; and war went out of fashion and Magniac he went out of his mind because he said he couldn't serve his country any more.
claims.description: War between nations has gone out of fashion by 2000, making military inventions obsolete.

claims.quote: The Mark Boat signals we must attend to the derelict, now whistling her death-song, as she falls beneath us in long sick zigzags.
claims.description: Stationary 'Mark Boat' airships mid-ocean serve as air-traffic control and rescue coordination, and crews rescue people using transporter slings.

claims.quote: Captain Hodgson opens the underbody colloid, swings the heavy pithing-iron out of its rack which in liners is generally cased as a smoking-room settee, and at two hundred feet releases the catch.
claims.description: Derelict airships are destroyed with a dropped 'pithing-iron' with opening crescent arms to prevent hazards to traffic.

claims.quote: if one disturbs the High Gods' market-rates by hurling steel hulls at ninety knots across tremblingly adjusted electric tensions, one must not complain of any rudeness in the reception.
claims.description: The upper atmosphere has electrical tension layers, vortices and blow-outs that airships must navigate, and skin friction can discharge them.

claims.quote: The inner skin shuts off fifty feet of the bow and as much of the stern, but the bow-bulkhead is recessed for the lift-shunting apparatus
claims.description: Lift-shunt devices remove lift from the gas to control altitude, letting ships trim by tanks and rudder.

claims.quote: Our shaft-bearings are C.M.C. (Commercial Minerals Company) stones, ground with as much care as the lens of a telescope.
claims.description: Engine bearings are made from precisely ground jewels, replacing cheaper enamel compounds.

claims.quote: What if that wavering carcass had been filled with the men of the old days, each one of them taught (that is the horror of it!) that, after death he would very possibly go for ever to unspeakable torment?
claims.description: By 2000, religious belief in eternal damnation has faded from society.

claims.quote: These bearings came from “No. 97,” which took them over from the old Dominion of Light which had them out of the wreck of the Persew aeroplane in the years when men still flew wooden kites over oil engines!
claims.description: Early heavier-than-air aeroplanes with oil engines are obsolete by 2000, superseded by gas-lifted airships.
